chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhl, from a man, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Verily, the owl fasts during the day, and when it breaks its fast, it laments over al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) until morning.

key_terms.عَلَى: Over / upon (in the context of mourning)

ai.seo_question: What do owls do after breaking their fast according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* illustrates the concept of *al-Balaa'* (cosmic resonance), where creation reflects the spiritual reality of the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically linking the owl's daily cycle to the perpetual mourning for Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). It underscores the Shia belief that nature itself participates in the commemoration of the Ahl al-Bayt's sacrifices, reinforcing the idea that the tragedy of Karbala transcends human history to become a universal event. This serves as a theological basis for the deep emotional connection Shia Muslims feel toward the natural world during the months of Muharram and Safar.
